Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{AB}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{EB}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{EC}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{DC}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{CB}$ in terms of vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{CB}=$    
 {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $C$ to $B$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{CB}=\overset{\to }{CE}+\overset{\to }{EB},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/1c1826cfb7602c6380fed1e2aa3c380f575a29185c46ca969d212d94f7c11aed.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{CE}=-c,\,\overset{\to }{EB}=b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/c013029af2f1d0dd727ac3c2dc701334fe51a9391b9691144a12f4cfff25c3d5.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CB} & =\overset{\to }{CE}+\overset{\to }{EB} \\  & =-c+b \\  & =b-c.\end{aligned}
$$
